intra-operative cytology improves the accuracy of pre-operative fine needle aspiration and frozen section diagnosis of thyroid and breast lesions.
the combined use of FNAC and intraoperative cytology improves the diagnostic accuracy for breast and thyroid lesions.

the combination of preoperative FNAC and IC is more accurate than FS alone in diagnosing breast and thyroid lesions and should be considered as the preferred method for intraoperative diagnosis of such lesions in the future.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of intraoperative fine needle aspiration and frozen section in the diagnosis of thyroid lesions and breast masses.
the study of the effect of fine needle aspiration cytological (FNAC) examination and intraoperative cytology and frozen sections (ICFS) in the diagnosis of breast lumps and thyroid lesions.
the role of intraoperative imprint cytology (IC) in the diagnosis of breast masses and thyroid lesions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IC is a very important tool in surgical decision-making, particularly in thyroid and breast surgery.
IC and FS are complementary techniques that improve the overall accuracy of the preoperative diagnosis.
IC is a very useful adjunct to FS in the intraoperative diagnosis of breast and thyroid lesions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of FNAC, intraoperative imprint cytology and frozen sections is a reliable diagnostic tool in the evaluation of breast and thyroid lesions.
IC and FNAC are both useful in the evaluation of breast masses.
the combination of FNAC and IC is the best approach in the diagnosis of breast lesions and the combination of IC and FS is the best approach for thyroid lesions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IC is a simple, rapid, cost effective and accurate method that can be used as a complementary tool to FNAC and FS.

the combination of pre-operative fine needle aspiration cytological (FNAC) diagnosis with intra-operative cytological diagnosis (IC) is a reliable and cost-effective method of diagnosing breast and thyroid lesions, and that the combination of intra-operative cytological (IC) diagnosis with intraoperative frozen section is a reliable method of diagnosing thyroid lesions, and may be used in cases where FNAC has failed to diagnose a thyroid lesion.
IC should be performed in every case in which a definitive diagnosis is required during operation.
